title: vLLM
subtitle: vLLM is the engine ActiveKV lives inside, patched at the scheduler, worker and attention backend, and the server under my local open-source models.

stats.label: token histories for a 27B hybrid model on one card
the single card it runs on
more sustained throughput than a mixed 4-bit/8-bit control

lede: ActiveKV began with a limit I kept hitting in vLLM: it keeps a model's whole key-value cache for a request in GPU memory, and its offload is a prefix cache that reuses prompts it has seen. Once a request's history outgrew the card, the request could not continue. I treated prefix reuse and active-context tiering as separate problems from the start. I decided to move the history to host memory and keep it inside vLLM, at its own extension points, delivered as compiled binaries plus a patch to the user's own vLLM, so users keep their own engine. Attention history lives in pinned host memory and the card keeps a bounded working set.
quote: A flat throughput curve under concurrency now sends me to the client first.
evidence: vLLM internals: ActiveKV built into vLLM at its scheduler, key-value connector, worker, attention backend and plugin system, delivered as binaries plus a patch.
KV-cache offload for LLM inference: attention history in pinned host memory with a bounded working set on the card, 128,000-token histories for a 27B model on one 32 GB card.
LLM quantization (4-bit): a 27B model quantized to a format the stock XPU build serves, 36% more sustained throughput for 3% higher perplexity.
C++ and native ports with parity proof: the runtime moved from Python inside vLLM to native C++ with bit-identical output in every parity cell.
